title: Dynamic kernel hinting + thread isolation + adaptive prefetch throttle to cut host overhead
creator: Daniel Park
description: Problem: host-side overhead (CPU contention, bursty memcpy, and probe/kernel scheduling chatter) contributes a material fraction of p95 prefill+decode latency for short-to-medium sequence workloads. Prior tickets focused on threadpool and coalescing; this ticket experiments with a coordinated approach that combines lightweight dynamic kernel hinting, transient thread isolation for memcpy-heavy prefetch, and an adaptive prefetch throttle to smooth spikes.
acceptance_criteria: p95 host CPU time for prefill reduced by >=25% on representative short/medium sequence traces
memcpy peak frequency (events/sec) reduced by >=35% under synthetic spike workloads
no >5% regression in overall throughput on long-sequence benchmarks
automated canary run shows no correctness or memory-safety regressions; rollout gated behind feature flag
design_notes: 1) Kernel hinting: runtime exposes a per-request light-weight hint based on (seq_len_bucket, quantization_profile, is_cache_hit) passed to kernel selection. Hints bias the kernel picker toward lower-latency kernels for short sequences (e.g., favor fused attention where available) and towards quantization-friendly kernels for low-precision paths.

2) Thread isolation: introduce a 'memcpy-isolate' worker pool. Prefetch tasks that exceed a memcpy_desire_threshold are scheduled on this pool to avoid evicting latency-sensitive decode workers. Pool size is auto-scaled based on memcpy backlog metric.

3) Adaptive prefetch throttle: a control loop measures host memcpy queue length and p95 prefill latency; when thresholds are crossed it reduces prefetch concurrency (backoff), prioritizing critical decode paths. Throttle uses PID-lite smoothing to avoid oscillation.
4) Telemetry: add per-request micro-metrics (small fixed-size envelope) to decide hinting buckets without adding significant overhead. We aggregate at 1s resolution for scheduler decisions.

5) Fallbacks: if hinting information is unsupported for a model/runtime combo, kernel selection falls back to current stable heuristic. Feature gated behind 'host-overhead-reduction' flag for safe rollback.

Trade-offs: extra telemetry and isolation pools consume a small amount of memory and thread capacity; we expect net win on p95 latency for our target workloads. Complexity increases in scheduler code and must be covered by e2e and perf tests.
implementation_plan: A) Add kernel-hint API and lightweight hinting logic (2 days) - PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4742
B) Implement memcpy-isolate worker pool and scheduling hook (3 days) - PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4761
C) Implement adaptive prefetch throttle control loop and config knobs (2 days) - PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4770
D) Telemetry + dashboards: expose memcpy_queue_length, hint_distribution, prefill_p95; dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/host-overhead/host-overhead-summary
E) Benchmarks & canary: synthetic spike tests + real-customer trace replay (2 days). Canary on dedicated-small cluster behind feature flag.
F) Rollout: stage -> canary (5% traffic) -> 20% -> full in 1-2 days if metrics stable.
testing_plan: unit tests for kernel hinting logic and scheduler fallbacks
integration tests for memcpy-isolate worker pool under controlled load
perf harness: replay of 5 representative traces (short chat, code-complete, summarization, embeddings burst)
fault injection: simulate memcopy slowdowns and ensure throttle stabilizes without traffic loss
canary - confirm p95 improvements and zero correctness regressions
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: telemetry overhead could itself add CPU pressure. Mitigation: use fixed-size envelopes and sample 1/10 of requests in heavy clusters; roll back sampling if overhead seen.
Risk: oscillation from throttle. Mitigation: use smoothing + floor/ceil limits and short cooldown windows.
Risk: regressions for exotic model kernels. Mitigation: safe fallback to stable kernel path per-model and model opt-out list.
Risk: rollout impacts dedicated customers. Mitigation: default-off for Dedicated until validated in hosted small clusters; opt-in config for early testers.
notes: Initial microbench results (local): memcpy peak events down 42% when using memcpy-isolate + throttle; host p95 CPU time down ~28% on short-sequence workload (seq<=128). Long-sequence throughput unchanged within 2%.
